mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the following 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% over a two-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages for three months indicates a dual signal of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which increases uncertainty and reduces risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month average for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong, sustained increase in personal income (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in consumption (GDPC1), signals a savings-driven environment where consumers are not translating income gains into spending, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for 5 consecutive months AND GDPC1 not > 12-month MA
regime_hint: savings glut or precautionary behavior regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS is persistently above its 12-month MA while GDPC1 is not.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with a simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) over three months signals deepening labor market weakness, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts materials and homebuilding sector earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
